Subject: MAP: token waterfall + cost check before procurement

Marissa —

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday. Procurement asked me to get the unit-econ items nailed down in the MAP before we start routing paperwork. We have two asks up front:

1) Confirm tokens/$ assumption that will be applied in the pilot (we need a predictable cost envelope for our finance signoff).
2) Clarify caching/prefetch and batching assumptions — specifically around cache hit-rate expectations and max batch sizes that will be used in Dedicated vs Hosted during pilot.

We'd like the MAP to reflect acceptance criteria tied to cost (tokens per $) and a clear closure timeline so procurement can schedule the PO and DocuSign routing. Our timeline target is to have commercial terms signed by 31 May if possible.

Can you send a short confirmed unit-price waterfall and any supporting working files so we can validate with finance?

Best,
Anne

Luminis Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: MAP: token waterfall + cost check before procurement

Anne —

Thanks — attaching a revised MAP draft (rev 3) and the unit economics workbook for your finance team to review. High level answers below and a short waterfall summary in the attached PDF:

- Baseline token price used in pilot (hosted): $0.0009 per token-equivalent (this is the list unit we use in the MAP).
- Pilot expected effective tokens/$ (after batching + cache): 1,100 tokens per $ at our baseline traffic profile (50% prefix reuse, dynamic batching with average batch=8). This implies ~ $0.00091/token raw but effective ops gets you ~18% improvement after batching/caching.
- Caching assumptions: KV/prefix cache hit-rate expected 45% during the pilot window (we're conservative; many customers see 55–65% with warmed caches and prefetch). Prefetch strategy: warm top-300 prompt fragments, TTL 12h for pilot.
- Batching assumptions: dynamic batching enabled with max_batch_size=16, target avg_batch=6–10 depending on parallel requests; we recommend configuring a 100ms batching window for Luminis given your latency targets.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 450ms for single-turn generation under pilot throughput (50 rps). If you need lower P95, we can reserve Dedicated capacity.
- Pilot size & timeline: 2-week canary (5/19–6/2) limited to 10% traffic, full pilot (6/3–6/30) at agreed throughput. Contract/PO target: 31 May.

Attached: MAP_Draft_v3.pdf (shows acceptance criteria and token waterfall), unit_econ_assumptions.xlsx (detailed calc), token-waterfall-diagram.png.

Can you confirm finance would like higher-fidelity token samples (we can export an anonymized sample of tokenization for a 10k query slice)? Also looping in procurement if they have required invoice terms.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0183

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: token waterfall + cost check before procurement

Marissa —

Quick internal notes on the assumptions you shared (copied to Karthik for pricing/ops alignment):

> From: Marissa Cole — Baseline token price $0.0009 per token-equivalent

- Confirm whether that baseline is pre-quantization. If we expect customers to use our int8 quantized runtime, we should call out a quantization uplift (approx -9–12% cost) in the spreadsheet.
- Batching: agree with max_batch_size=16, but call out an ops-safe default of max_batch_size=12 for the canary. It keeps P95 headroom and avoids tail amplification on spikes. We'll show both scenarios in the workbook (12 vs 16).
- Caching: 45% hit-rate is defensible as a conservative baseline. Add an optimistic column (60% hit) for finance to see upside. Prefetch list: we'll provide the top-300 fragments export — added as a separate tab in the workbook.
- Measurement: include a single metric in MAP acceptance: "cost drift <= 12% vs modeled tokens/$" over the first 14 days. If drift >12% we trigger an engineering ops review (and a temporary cap on traffic).

I'll update the unit_econ_assumptions.xlsx with the quantization and alternate batch sizing. Karthik, please confirm the Dedicated reserve delta and the expected latency change if they opt for Dedicated.

Ben
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none — edits will be pushed to the shared workbook]

Anne / Procurement team —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is MAP_Draft_v3.pdf (finalized with Ben/Karthik inputs) and the updated unit_econ_assumptions.xlsx. Summary of what changed from my last note:

- Baseline list unit remains $0.0009/token-equivalent (pre-quantization).
- Two cost scenarios added to the MAP: Conservative (cache hit 45%, avg_batch=6, effective 1,100 tokens/$) and Optimistic (cache hit 60%, avg_batch=9, effective 1,400 tokens/$). Both scenarios include a quantization uplift line (expected -10% cost in our quantized runtime option).
- Canary config: max_batch_size=12, batching window=100ms, prefetch top-300 fragments, pilot limit 10% traffic. Acceptance metric: cost drift <=12% vs modeled tokens/$ over first 14 days.
- Timeline:
  - 5/19 — canary start (10% traffic)
  - 6/03 — full pilot (agreed throughput)
  - 6/30 — pilot end & acceptance readout
  - Commercial signature target: 5/31 (PO/DocuSign)

Next steps we need from Luminis:
1) Procurement: confirm DocuSign routing and payment terms (Net30/Net45). If Proc needs a different billing cadence, let us know; we'll reflect it in the MAP.
2) Finance: greenlight either Conservative or Optimistic scenario for the MAP cost envelope. If you want anonymized token samples we can export a 10k query sample (redacted).
3) Ops: sign the canary guardrails section (we will throttle automatically if cost drift >12%).

Links: HubSpot HS-2025-LH-47 (internal record), shared MAP: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aB2cExample

If procurement confirms DocuSign routing today, we'll send the final DocuSign packet with the MAP embedded and a short one-page summary for exec signoff.
